title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, partly conjectural: this is the 'équation des lacets' cycle (Grothendieck's own folio 516), the continuation of La Longue Marche. In this cycle Γ_Q^~ is Grothendieck's candidate group for the action of Gal(Q̄/Q), defined by the loop equations. It is close to what Drinfeld and Ihara later called \hat{GT}. Here it appears as γ_{ρ,σ}.

The setup from the previous page:
- M is a large profinite group (an automorphism or extension group) mapping onto γ_{ρ,σ} = Γ_Q^~.
- ρ is an element of order 3 (the next page gives L_{-ρ} ≅ Z/3Z), and L_ρ is the subgroup it generates. σ is presumably the order-2 partner, recalling PSL_2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3.
- M^! is a normal subgroup and μ ≅ μ_2 = {±1}.
- Z_ρ = Cent_M(L_ρ), Z_ρ^! = Z_ρ ∩ M^!, and Z^!_{ρ,0} = M'(-j).
- By (18), M → γ_{ρ,σ} maps Z^!_{ρ,0} isomorphically onto γ'_{ρ,σ} = ker(ε_3). Here ε_3 is a ±1-valued character, plausibly the mod-3 cyclotomic character.
- By (19), Z_ρ^! ≅ M'(-j) × μ.

This page, equations (20)-(22):
1. Take the order-2 subgroup μ_{τ'} = {1, τ'}, where τ' is an involution with τ'(ρ) = ρ^{-1} (a 'complex conjugation'-type element).
2. Since τ' inverts ρ, it normalizes L_ρ. Hence it normalizes the centralizer Z_ρ, and therefore Z_ρ^! = Z_ρ ∩ M^!, because M^! is normal in M.
3. Since μ_{τ'} ∩ M^! = {1}, the group N_ρ^? := μ_{τ'}·Z_ρ^! is a semidirect product μ_{τ'} ⋉ (Z^!_{ρ,0} × μ), with Z^!_{ρ,0} × μ ≅ Γ'^~_Q × μ.
4. Warning: τ' does not normalize the factor Z^!_{ρ,0}. So one does not get a decomposition N_ρ^? = N^?_{ρ,0} × μ with N^?_{ρ,0} = μ_{τ'}·Z^!_{ρ,0}, contrary to what the notation suggests.
5. Exact sequence (22): 1 → μ → N_ρ^? → γ_{ρ,σ} (= Γ_Q^~) → 1.
6. So N_ρ^? is a 'quasi-section of multiplicity 2' of M → γ_{ρ,σ}: a subgroup surjecting onto the quotient with kernel of order 2.

The next page then writes M and N_ρ as amalgamated products of N_ρ^? with known groups over μ_2. It also notes that the action of τ on Z^!_ρ should be made explicit, guessing that it involves ε_2.

Purpose: to split the big extension M of Γ_Q^~ as far as possible. One finds a near-section through the centralizer of an order-3 element, extended by a complex-conjugation-like involution. This helps describe the structure of the Teichmüller-type group in terms of Γ_Q^~ (the GT-like group).
errors: Step 5 (surjectivity with kernel exactly μ) is implicit, not argued. It requires: the image of τ' lies outside γ'_{ρ,σ} = ker ε_3 (true if ε_3 detects inversion of ρ); ε_3 has image of order 2, so γ' has index 2; and μ lies in ker(M → γ_{ρ,σ}). Under these assumptions the argument is correct. Kernel = (Z_ρ^! ∩ ker) = μ, since Z^!_{ρ,0} maps injectively, and elements τ'z map outside γ'.

The equation labels are inconsistent with the surrounding pages. The previous page ends at (19) and the next page cites (22) and (23). So the labels here should be (20), (21), (22), not (28), (29), (30).
In (21), M(-j̄) under the brace should be M'(-j̄), per (17)/(18). The struck alternative '≃ MΓ_Q × μ' was abandoned by Grothendieck.

ideas.what: An involution inverting an order-3 element normalizes its centralizer. This gives a semidirect product μ_{τ'} ⋉ Z_ρ^!.
A subgroup of M surjecting onto Γ_Q^~ with kernel μ_2 ('quasi-section of multiplicity 2'). It is built from the centralizer of an order-3 element plus a 'complex conjugation'.
ideas.modern_name: Lifting \hat{GT} (or Gal(Q̄/Q)) to automorphism groups of profinite SL_2(Z)/B_3 up to the center ±1; GT-actions fixing torsion elements of the modular group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related work: Drinfeld, Ihara (\hat{GT}), Lochak–Schneps (GT and automorphisms of braid groups), Nakamura, Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki. The exact construction here: unsure
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the GT/Teichmüller tower idea; this construction is unpublished

ideas.what: Caution that the decomposition does not respect the product structure, since τ' does not normalize Z^!_{ρ,0}. Plus the guess (next page) that the twisting cocycle Γ'^~_Q → μ is ε_2.
ideas.modern_name: Non-split / twisted central extension by ±1; action of complex conjugation on the GT-lift

missed.claim: Grothendieck constructs a canonical index-2-kernel 'quasi-section' N_ρ^? of M → Γ_Q^~ via the centralizer of an order-3 element and a ρ-inverting involution. On the next page he leaves open the explicit action of τ' on Z_ρ^! ≅ Γ'^~_Q × μ, conjecturing it is governed by ε_2. This is a concrete, checkable statement about the ±1 central extension of (a version of) \hat{GT}. I do not know of a place in the literature where it is stated in this form.
missed.quote: de sorte que N_ρ^? est une quasi-section de multiplicité 2 de l'extension N_ρ^∧ → γ_{ρ,σ}, ou de M → γ_{ρ,σ} = Γ_Q^~
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Explicit lifts of \hat{GT} or G_Q into automorphism groups of profinite SL_2(Z)/B_3 bear on studies of GT-actions on modular-group torsion and on anabelian reconstruction (e.g. Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki). They also bear on the role of complex conjugation in GT. Whether this specific ±1 extension and its cocycle (ε_2?) have been worked out is unclear.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is careful but routine group-theoretic bookkeeping inside Grothendieck's unpublished GT/Teichmüller computations. The 'multiplicity-2 quasi-section' is a mildly interesting structural detail, but its novelty is hard to assess without the definitions of M and M^!.
transcription_corrections: Equation labels read (20), (21), (22) in the image, not (28), (29), (30). This is consistent with the previous page ending at (19) and the next page citing (22) and (23).
'516' at top is Grothendieck's own page number.
'on il n'en est rien' should read 'or il n'en est rien'.
Under the brace in (21) the image reads 'M(-j̄)×μ ≃ Γ'^~_Q × μ'; the intended object is M'(-j̄).
In 'μ_{τ'} ne normalise [-pas-] Z^!_{ρ,o}', the struck token sits before Z (an '≠'/'pas'-like mark). The sense is that τ' does NOT normalize Z^!_{ρ,0}.
